verses.en: Is there not an appointed time to man upon earth? are not his days also like the days of an hireling?
verses.pt: Porventura não tem o homem duro serviço sobre a terra? E não são os seus dias como os do jornaleiro?
verses.en_web: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?
verses.en_bbe: Has not man his ordered time of trouble on the earth? and are not his days like the days of a servant working for payment?

verses.en: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for the reward of his work:
verses.pt: Como o escravo que suspira pela sombra, e como o jornaleiro que espera pela sua paga,
verses.en_web: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,
verses.en_bbe: As a servant desiring the shades of evening, and a workman looking for his payment:

verses.en: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.
verses.pt: assim se me deram meses de escassez, e noites de aflição se me ordenaram.
verses.en_web: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.
verses.en_bbe: So I have for my heritage months of pain to no purpose, and nights of weariness are given to me.

verses.en: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.
verses.pt: Havendo-me deitado, digo: Quando me levantarei? Mas comprida é a noite, e farto-me de me revolver na cama até a alva.
verses.en_web: When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.
verses.en_bbe: When I go to my bed, I say, When will it be time to get up? but the night is long, and I am turning from side to side till morning light.

verses.en: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.
verses.pt: A minha carne se tem vestido de vermes e de torrões de pó; a minha pele endurece, e torna a rebentar-se.
verses.en_web: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
verses.en_bbe: My flesh is covered with worms and dust; my skin gets hard and then is cracked again.

verses.en: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
verses.pt: Os meus dias são mais velozes do que a lançadeira do tecelão, e chegam ao fim sem esperança.
verses.en_web: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.
verses.en_bbe: My days go quicker than the cloth-worker's thread, and come to an end without hope.

verses.en: O remember that my life is wind: mine eye shall no more see good.
verses.pt: Lembra-te de que a minha vida é um sopro; os meus olhos não tornarão a ver o bem.
verses.en_web: Oh remember that my life is a breath. My eye shall no more see good.
verses.en_bbe: O, keep in mind that my life is wind: my eye will never again see good.

verses.en: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no more: thine eyes are upon me, and I am not.
verses.pt: Os olhos dos que agora me vêem não me verão mais; os teus olhos estarão sobre mim, mas não serei mais.
verses.en_web: The eye of him who sees me shall see me no more. Your eyes shall be on me, but I shall not be.
verses.en_bbe: The eye of him who sees me will see me no longer: your eyes will be looking for me, but I will be gone.

verses.en: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more.
verses.pt: Tal como a nuvem se desfaz e some, aquele que desce à sepultura nunca tornará a subir.
verses.en_web: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to Sheol shall come up no more.
verses.en_bbe: A cloud comes to an end and is gone; so he who goes down into the underworld comes not up again.

verses.en: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
verses.pt: Nunca mais tornará à sua casa, nem o seu lugar o conhecerá mais.
verses.en_web: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
verses.en_bbe: He will not come back to his house, and his place will have no more knowledge of him.

verses.en: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.pt: Por isso não reprimirei a minha boca; falarei na angústia do meu espírito, queixar-me-ei na amargura da minha alma.
verses.en_web: “Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.en_bbe: So I will not keep my mouth shut; I will let the words come from it in the pain of my spirit, my soul will make a bitter outcry.

verses.en: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?
verses.pt: Sou eu o mar, ou um monstro marinho, para que me ponhas uma guarda?
verses.en_web: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
verses.en_bbe: Am I a sea, or a sea-beast, that you put a watch over me?

verses.en: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;
verses.pt: Quando digo: Confortar-me-á a minha cama, meu leito aliviará a minha queixa,
verses.en_web: When I say, ‘My bed shall comfort me. My couch shall ease my complaint;’
verses.en_bbe: When I say, In my bed I will have comfort, there I will get rest from my disease;

verses.en: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions:
verses.pt: então me espantas com sonhos, e com visões me atemorizas;
verses.en_web: then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions:
verses.en_bbe: Then you send dreams to me, and visions of fear;

verses.en: So that my soul chooseth strangling, and death rather than my life.
verses.pt: de modo que eu escolheria antes a estrangulação, e a morte do que estes meus ossos.
verses.en_web: so that my soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.
verses.en_bbe: So that a hard death seems better to my soul than my pains.

verses.en: I loathe it; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days are vanity.
verses.pt: A minha vida abomino; não quero viver para sempre; retira-te de mim, pois os meus dias são vaidade.
verses.en_web: I loathe my life. I don’t want to live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
verses.en_bbe: I have no desire for life, I would not be living for ever! Keep away from me, for my days are as a breath.

verses.en: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?
verses.pt: Que é o homem, para que tanto o engrandeças, e ponhas sobre ele o teu pensamento,
verses.en_web: What is man, that you should magnify him, that you should set your mind on him,
verses.en_bbe: What is man, that you have made him great, and that your attention is fixed on him,

verses.en: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?
verses.pt: e cada manhã o visites, e cada momento o proves?
verses.en_web: that you should visit him every morning, and test him every moment?
verses.en_bbe: And that your hand is on him every morning, and that you are testing him every minute?

verses.en: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
verses.pt: Até quando não apartarás de mim a tua vista, nem me largarás, até que eu possa engolir a minha saliva?
verses.en_web: How long will you not look away from me, nor leave me alone until I swallow down my spittle?
verses.en_bbe: How long will it be before your eyes are turned away from me, so that I may have a minute's breathing-space?

verses.en: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?
verses.pt: Se peco, que te faço a ti, ó vigia dos homens? Por que me fizeste alvo dos teus dardos? Por que a mim mesmo me tornei pesado?
verses.en_web: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?
verses.en_bbe: If I have done wrong, what have I done to you, O keeper of men? why have you made me a mark for your blows, so that I am a weariness to myself?

verses.en: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.
verses.pt: Por que me não perdoas a minha transgressão, e não tiras a minha iniqüidade? Pois agora me deitarei no pó; tu me buscarás, porém eu não serei mais.
verses.en_web: Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust. You will seek me diligently, but I shall not be.”
verses.en_bbe: And why do you not take away my sin, and let my wrongdoing be ended? for now I go down to the dust, and you will be searching for me with care, but I will be gone.
